figures.caption: Table 1: The default agent team. Five agents carry out the research; the Auditor checks the team’s output before delivery.

Table 2: Agents’ Last Exam scores, runtime, and cost by harness × backbone. Within each task, õ− and õ+ denote domain knowledge disabled and enabled, respectively (T1 skull-stripping QC, T2 ROI resampling, T3 C. elegans tracking; Appendix C). Runtime and cost correspond to õ+. Green marks full credit (1.00) on T1 and T2; T3 has no pass threshold. “F” marks a failed task with no gradable deliverable. Each score reports a single run graded against a withheld reference.

Table 3: BrainPilotBench performance, runtime, and cost by harness × backbone. Within each task, õ− and õ+ denote domain knowledge disabled and enabled, respectively. Time and cost are summed over all four tasks with domain knowledge enabled. Costs are in US dollars using official provider list prices verified on 16 July 2026, consistent with the ALE analysis. For BrainPilot, RSC reports the higher-scoring of two runs, with shorter runtime as the tie-breaker; all other cells report one formal run. “F” means that no valid primary score was produced and is not numerical zero.

Figure 7: Case study: spatial coding in the retrosplenial cortex. (a) Representative single-cell activity heatmaps with spatial tuning curves. (b) Population firing-rate map of detected place cells, sorted on odd trials and rendered on held-out even trials. (c) Bayesian position decoding: trueversus-decoded scatter and row-normalized confusion matrix. (d) True and decoded positions across held-out test trials. (e) Trial-bin population-vector correlation matrix. (f) Peak-position drift and population mean peak rate across trials.

Figure 9: Case study: an fMRI pain connectivity signature and its transfer. (a) Full FC weight matrix of the learned signature. (b) Pain-region network of the signature weights. (c) Held-out true-versus-predicted pain ratings in the experimental tonic-pain cohort. (d) External regression of signature response against pain severity in the clinical back-pain cohort. (e) Chronic-back-pain versus healthy-control classification in the Japan and UK cohorts, shown using ROC curves and signature-response distributions.

Figure 10: Case study: EEG motor-imagery decoding on BCI Competition IV 2a. (a) Model comparison (MIAgentModel vs. EEGNet baseline). (b) Learned spatial filters as scalp topographies. (c) Class activation topomaps (subject 3). (d) Right-minus-left contrast (subject 3). (e) Class topomaps and contrast (subject 9). (f) Temporal-kernel FFT with Mu and Beta bands highlighted.

Figure 11: Case study: Sleep-EDF downstream sleep-staging decoder with physiological validation. (a) 20-fold leave-one-subject-out curves with DeepSleepNet reference lines. (b) Class-wise power spectral density. (c) Relative band-power heatmap across the five stages. (d) Held-out confusion matrix and per-class F1. (e) True-versus-predicted hypnograms and transition matrices. (f) Temporal-kernel FFT and saliency examples.

Table 4: Per-run statistics for the BrainPilotBench RSC task. õ− and õ+ denote domain knowledge disabled and enabled, respectively. Time is agent wall-clock time and cost is calculated from input, output, cache-read, and cache-write tokens using official provider list prices verified on 16 July 2026. MCP, Search, and Load count domain-MCP calls, keyword skill searches, and complete skill loads, respectively. BrainPilot rows report the higher-scoring of two runs, with shorter runtime as the tie-breaker. “F” denotes the absence of a valid primary score, not a score of zero.
Table 5: Per-run statistics for TOPS-fMRI. Time, cost, token accounting, and resource-call definitions follow Table 4.
Table 6: Per-run statistics for BCI Competition IV 2a. “F” denotes the absence of a valid primary score; the valid 0.00 entries are retained.
Table 7: Per-run statistics for Sleep-EDF. All 14 submissions produced valid primary scores; 0.00 denotes a scored result.
Table 8: The three evaluated Agents’ Last Exam tasks. The grader scores each deliverable against a withheld reference revealed only after the run.
Table 9: Per-task cost ($) with domain knowledge enabled, by configuration.
Table 10: Per-task cost ($) and total runtime with domain knowledge disabled; same configurations and pricing as Table 2.
